summary: Ready device expert cache: the directory on the device (capture-safe layer plans and fills from a mapped bundle store), a prompt staging ring that never admits, KV lending, residency-profile warm start, admission limits that send misses to a CPU tier, ranked background swaps, telemetry, and portable policy replay
implementation_scope: CUDA/HIP warp planner with pinned clock replacement, admission limits (quota, quota by miss count, second-touch) that bypass misses to the store, bundle copies, lookahead prefetch and profile preload; ExpertCache runtime owning the directory and per-layer scratch with one capturable plan_and_fetch per routed layer and telemetry (expert_reads, expert_hits, bypassed); Metal versions of the kernels; Python directory reference; residency profile builder with a held-out check; CPU/link split table from measured layer times. Independent portable replay compares LRU/LFU/clock/hindsight eviction and optional second-touch admission over arbitrary byte-sized bundles. Expert arithmetic (device and CPU), the predictor and phase switching remain engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: Routed experts live in device-readable host memory behind a device slot cache, and per-layer host round trips dominate short decode steps; use portable replay to screen replacement/admission policies on retained demand traces before native adaptation
agent_guidance.avoid_when: All experts fit on the device, the host plan already overlaps device work, or large prefill batches touch most experts of a layer anyway
provides: Device directory arrays with stamp pins, clock hand, failure flag and hit/miss/pool counters
One-warp plan of up to 32 distinct routes per group with hits pinned before any admission
Warp-parallel clock victims identical to scanning one slot at a time
Copy jobs from the store or from a tagged prefetch pool, and a multi-block bundle copy kernel
Lookahead prefetch planner over a two-half pool selected by group parity
Host reference ClockDirectory and a hit-rate simulator for recorded routing traces
Offline byte-budget replay with grouped hit pins, exact bypass, warmup-excluded scores, fetch bytes and optional additive measured miss costs
LRU, cumulative LFU, clock and farthest-next-use comparison from identical input; always or second-touch admission
Capacity changes with atomic refusal under live pins; independent pin owners and explicit frequency decay
Prefill reuse/population policy, recent decode protection and phase/demand/draft/prefetch costs with unused versus wasted prefetch bytes
Admission limits on the device: a quota per plan, a quota by miss count (the CPU/link split) and second-touch; a bypassed miss takes no victim and its Use names the store bundle
Warm start: enqueue_preload maps a residency profile's keys to the first slots, unreferenced
ExpertCache: directory allocation and clearing, set_admission, preload, one capturable plan_and_fetch per routed layer, prefetch and telemetry with expert_reads/expert_hits
Residency profiles from router logs of a general corpus, with the corpus recorded and a cold-versus-preloaded held-out check on several traces
A quota table by miss count from link, CPU and combined layer timings measured on the target, never interpolated, with a recalibration check on the hit rate
A named general corpus for residency profiles (corpus.json): web text in seven languages and code in three to tune on, held-out sources to check on, fetched with revisions recorded
The host store: per-expert tensors (or stacked ones) packed once into one contiguous bundle per key with an index and the checkpoint's fingerprint, then pinned by registering the mapped file

A provider grouped GEMM's pointer arrays (per-component matrices inside each bundle, activation and output rows, routing weights) written on the device from a plan's Uses, bypassed misses optionally left to the CPU

Background ranked residency: route counts on the device, a policy ranking decayed counts of every layer together, swaps begun at a fixed window boundary on a side stream and committed at the next, so the cache adapts off the step's critical path and one request history always gives the same placement
Device form (experts:cache): ExpertCache.plan(layer, ids) over a step's routes, one plan launch then one fill launch, capture-safe; slot tables of slots, -1 not routed and -2 the CPU tier

A prompt ring: long chunks stage every non-resident expert of a layer by the copy engine, the next layer under the current one, events guarding each segment; short chunks copy their routed misses into ring slots
KV lending: the KV pool's pages no sequence holds are slots of the same store tensor, reclaimed before the pool hands them out
BundleStore (experts:store): bundles in registered host memory with a device view, read-only registration of a store file

CSF-compressed NVFP4 scales kept compressed in the store (csf_layout, csf_bundle) and decoded into the slot layout by the fill (a program of component copies and slab decodes), plus csf_decode / csf_encode on the host or the device
engine_supplies: Initial directory contents and the switch to and from host planning phases
Router outputs, the provider's grouped GEMM (fed by enqueue_operands) and the lookahead predictor
Side-stream fork after the group's own fill and the join before the next plan
Checking the failure flag before trusting a step
Complete demand groups, content/representation-keyed bundle extents, measured miss costs where available, held-out traces and actual execution validation
Faithful phase/traffic events, explicit lifetime pins valid for each policy, and actual capacity/aging schedules
CPU computation (or mapped reads) of bypassed misses, with the device's bits where batch invariance applies (host-expert-arithmetic)
Router logs of a general corpus unrelated to Eval and held-out traces for a residency profile, and the layer timing callables for split calibration
The component templates naming the checkpoint's expert tensors and scales, and the bundle alignment its expert kernels need
preserve: Every route of a plan is pinned against that plan's admissions
Copies complete before arithmetic reads a slot; a key maps to at most one slot
The pool half being consumed is not refilled before its plan
Host and device apply the same replacement rule when both plan
Replay misses always retain exact demand identity; unknown costs stay unknown; hindsight results and additive miss costs are not online throughput evidence
Accepted and rejected draft labels use identical online replacement decisions; hindsight is confined to farthest-next-use
Refused capacity shrink does not partially evict live content or change the budget
The cache keeps adapting during decode: link-fetched experts are admitted, and replacement is not frozen after a warmup or profile load
adapt: Replacement policy that respects pins, bundle layout and copy granularity
Blocks per copy, prefetch width and predictor
Mapped reads versus DMA copies, and graph capture boundaries
Offline byte budgets, replacement/admission policies and warmup; native policy changes still require host/device parity and lifetime validation
The CPU/link miss split: the quota table from split.py, measured on the target machine alone and together, recalibrated as the hit rate moves
Whether second-touch admission and lookahead prefetch stay on, by integrated decode measurements

requires.hardware: CUDA C++20 with device-readable host memory for the store; Python 3.11+ standard library for the reference; portable replay uses only Python's standard library and needs no device; HIP (AMD) and Metal (Apple) sources of the C++ component beside the CUDA one, not run in crit's tests. The device form needs torch: directory_ops.cu built at load for the device's architecture (all of sm_80..121a compile; CUDA only, torch's builder would hipify it on ROCm, untested), the torch ops anywhere torch runs (CPU included)
requires.model: Routed experts as fixed-size bundles (a multiple of 16 bytes); the C++ component plans at most 32 distinct routes per call, the device form any routes of a step (duplicates and -1 allowed) of up to a few thousand experts a layer (9 bytes of shared memory per expert); offline replay accepts arbitrary complete bundle sizes and group widths
requires.workload: Decode steps where host planning latency per routed layer is significant and expert reuse is high; replay also supports recorded grouped accesses under byte pressure independently of CUDA geometry

contract.input: Directory pointers and geometry; group index; device route ids and optional weights; predicted ids for prefetch; replay takes ordered complete demand groups, exact bundle keys/extents, optional miss costs, a byte budget and warmup prefix; optional Demand phase/traffic labels and Capacity, Decay, Pin and Release events; admission quota, quota table by miss count and second-touch; profile keys for preload; measured layer timings for the split
contract.output: Use per route (slot or store bundle, key, weight, source); copy jobs and their count; updated directory, pool tags and counters; replay returns distinct-demand hit/miss scores, fetch bytes, admission/bypass/eviction counts, optional additive cost and peak retained bytes; initial/final capacity, refused shrinks, phase/traffic counters and wasted/unused prefetch bytes; ExpertCache telemetry (hits, misses, pooled, prefetched, bypassed, failure flag); profiles with held-out hit rates; quota tables
contract.ownership: The engine owns every array, the store, slots and pool; kernels borrow them on the caller's stream; uses stay valid until a later plan of the same directory evicts the slot. Replay copies input metadata into private analysis state and owns no physical allocations. ExpertCache owns the directory arrays and per-layer scratch it allocates; slots, pool and store stay the engine's.
contract.failure: Launches reject invalid geometry, more than 32 or more than slot-count routes and null pointers; on the device an out-of-range or duplicate route sets state[2] = 1 and yields a null use; a plan without a victim sets state[2] = 2. Replay rejects unknown keys, invalid budgets/extents/costs or policies; insufficient admission space bypasses without partial eviction and still charges the exact miss. Invalid/nonresident pins and unknown releases fail; impossible shrink is reported atomically.
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; Core supplies allocations, streams and readiness; residency policy stays with the engine

dependencies: Python standard library for the reference

validation.host: ClockDirectory pins hits before admissions, chooses clock victims, copies predicted misses from the pool, rejects duplicates and out-of-range routes; byte replay checks variable sizes, grouped pins, second-touch, warmup and missing costs; randomized clock comparison against ClockDirectory and exhaustive equal-size single-demand mandatory-admission hindsight oracle; capacity/pin atomicity and ownership, growth, aging, phase isolation, warmup control boundaries and speculative outcome independence; admission quota, quota table and second-touch bypasses without eviction; preload order, skips and clock start; profile key order, held-out check and geometry checks; split choice, ties, unmeasured counts and calibration calls; corpus manifest disjointness, paged fetch, cache and corpus statement; store packing of per-expert and stacked tensors, alignment, reuse on an unchanged source and refusals; ranked residency: ties by key, empty slots first, bursts, decay, reserved slots never victims, commits that find the key resident elsewhere, and a schedule whose hit rate recovers after a topic change with no admission on the step's path
validation.native: 600 random plans with lookahead prefetch on 24 and 72 slots against a host replica: identical slots, hit/miss/pool counters, complete bundle bytes, duplicate-route flag and rejected launches; ExpertCache on 20 and 40 slots: preload, 400 plans under a quota table and second-touch, bypassed store bundles, bytes and telemetry against the replica; enqueue_operands: component, activation and output pointers and weights from a plan's Uses, bypassed routes null; expert_store_tests.cpp: a store file pinned and read back through its device address; ranked residency on 16 and 40 slots: route counts, swaps, slots and bundle bytes at every boundary against the replica driven by a second policy, every miss bypassed, the hit rate climbing after a topic change. Passes on an RTX 5090; the device form (tests/test_device.py): the directory's CUDA ops and torch ops against LayerDirectory bit for bit over random route streams (duplicates, -1, invalid routes, unavailable slots, quotas, quota by miss count, second touch, failures, per-row counters), prompt plans, slots byte-exact against the store, a captured plan and fill replayed, prompt chunks reading staged bundles under a slow consumer, preload, the CPU tier quota, ranked swaps and KV lending over attention-state's pool; tests/test_csf.py: csf_decode against csf_encode and an independent encoder, on the host and the device; a CSF store's slots byte-exact in the slot layout through the CUDA program fill and the torch ops, in plans, a captured plan, a prompt chunk and a preload
